svg.title: One window through the state-space block
svg.desc: The example window 2+3=|5. through the trained SS01 block: the argmax next token at every position beside the target, a chip per position whose opacity is the share of that position still present in the last state (the mean decay raised to the distance), and the 32-value state at every position as a heat strip.
svg.text: ONE WINDOW -- the state carried along the window, decaying
WHAT: window 2+3=|5., positions 0..6; the state at position t holds a decayed sum of every earlier position's input.
state s_t [7, 32] after each position (shade = |value| / max)
state at position 4 (the bar), first 6 of 32: 0.78 0.39 0.38 0.91 -0.52 -1.13
WHY: a state-space block has no lookup back to an earlier position; whatever the answer needs must still be in the state when
the bar arrives. The chips show how much of each position the learned decay keeps by the end of the window.
HOW: ssm/state/example is u:ssm_states on the normalized embedding of this window; ssm/survival/example is mean(a^(6-t));
ssm/logits/example-argmax is the head's argmax at every position; the live demo replays the same recorded values.
Highlighted cells are graded positions where the argmax equals the target. Ids are alphabet indices (u:domain_alphabet).
Prediction cells are teacher-forced: each position sees the true prefix through the state.
